A cardiac flatline, also known as asystole, is a state where there is no electrical activity in the heart, resulting in no heartbeat. Defibrillation is a treatment used to correct certain types of abnormal heart rhythms, specifically ventricular fibrillation (VF) and pulseless ventricular tachycardia (VT), by delivering an electric shock to the heart to restore a normal rhythm.

However, in the case of asystole (cardiac flatline), defibrillation is not recommended because there is no erratic electrical activity to reset. Instead, the recommended treatment is high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and administration of medications like epinephrine to try to stimulate the heart.

Therefore, defibrillation is not used for a cardiac flatline; CPR is the recommended approach.
